formation.example: 갈 수 있어요 / 먹을 수 없어요

items.register: Only with movement verbs such as 가다, 오다, 다니다.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: I'll do it (promise or decision, considering the listener)
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: noun modifiers: turn a verb or adjective into a description of a noun
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.register: Can sound like an order to someone older or senior; use -(으)ㄹ까요? or -(으)시죠 instead.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: sequence: do A, then do B (B builds on A: same place or same object)

contrasts.note: -고 simply lists actions; -아/어서 links them so the second happens at the place or with the thing from the first (친구를 만나서 밥을 먹었어요).

items.register: Neutral; very common in speech and writing.
items.commonMistake: Tense goes only on the last verb: ✗ 학교에 갔어서 공부했어요 → ✓ 학교에 가서 공부했어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: reason: because, so (cause leading to a result)

contrasts.note: -(으)니까 can be followed by a request or suggestion; -아/어서 can't.

items.register: The natural choice for apologies and thanks: 늦어서 죄송합니다, 도와줘서 고마워요.
items.commonMistake: No past tense before it, and no command after it: ✗ 비가 와서 우산을 가져가세요 → ✓ 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: because, since (often a reason the speaker wants to stress)

contrasts.note: -아/어서 states a cause neutrally and can't take a command after it; -(으)니까 can (추우니까 창문 닫으세요).

items.register: With a verb of action it can also mean 'when I did A, I found B': 집에 가니까 아무도 없었어요.
items.commonMistake: Avoid it in apologies: ✗ 늦었으니까 죄송합니다 → ✓ 늦어서 죄송합니다.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ 후에 is the opposite: after doing.

items.commonMistake: No tense before -기: ✗ 잤기 전에 → ✓ 자기 전에.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -기 전에 is the opposite: before doing.
-고 나서 means much the same but stresses finishing A first.

items.register: -(으)ㄴ 다음에 and -(으)ㄴ 뒤에 mean the same.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄴ 후에 is a neutral 'after'; -고 나서 stresses that A is completely done.

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: try doing; in the past, have done (experience)
items.register: Very common in polite suggestions: 한번 입어 보세요.
items.commonMistake: In the past it means experience, not just an attempt: 가 봤어요 = I've been there.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: Often combined: -아/어 본 적이 있다 is the most natural way to say 'have tried'.

formation.example: 먹은 적이 있어요 / 가 본 적이 없어요

items.commonMistake: Not for routine things: ✗ 밥을 먹은 적이 있어요 sounds like eating rice is a rare event.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: oh, …! (reacting to something you just noticed)

contrasts.note: -군요 also marks realization but sounds more formal or written; -네요 is the everyday spoken choice.

items.commonMistake: ㄹ drops before ㄴ: ✗ 멀네요 → ✓ 머네요; ✗ 살네요 → ✓ 사네요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: …, right? (checking or stating something the listener should agree with)
items.register: In speech it is almost always shortened to -죠.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: in order to; intend to, be about to

contrasts.note: -(으)러 only goes with movement verbs (가다, 오다); -(으)려고 works with any verb.
-(으)ㄹ까 하다 is a vaguer 'thinking of maybe doing'.

items.commonMistake: ㄹ-stem verbs take -려고 directly: ✗ 만들으려고 → ✓ 만들려고.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.register: Usually in the past (했어요) because the decision is already made.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -는 동안 marks a period of time and the two subjects can differ; -(으)면서 needs the same subject.

items.commonMistake: Same subject for both parts: ✗ 제가 요리하면서 동생이 청소했어요 → ✓ 제가 요리하는 동안 동생이 청소했어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.register: With nouns, just add 때: 방학 때, 학생 때.
items.commonMistake: 갈 때 is before or on the way; 갔을 때 is after arriving: ✓ 한국에 갔을 때 친구를 만났어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: know / not know how to do

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 is about being able (including circumstances); -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 is about having learned the skill.

formation.example: 수영할 줄 알아요 / 운전할 줄 몰라요

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -(으)면 안 되다 is the opposite: must not.

items.register: As a question it asks permission: 들어가도 돼요?
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -아/어도 되다 is the opposite: may.

formation.example: 가면 안 돼요 / 먹으면 안 돼요

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: it seems (that); I think (softens an opinion)

contrasts.note: -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 is a guess about what will happen or what you can't see; -는 것 같다 is based on what is happening now.

items.register: Koreans use it a lot to sound less blunt, even about their own opinions: 이게 더 예쁜 것 같아요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: I think it will…; it looks like it'll…

contrasts.note: -는 것 같다 is based on present evidence; -(으)ㄹ 것 같다 is a prediction or a guess.
-(으)ㄹ 거예요 sounds more certain.

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: come to, end up (a change caused by circumstances, not your own choice)

contrasts.note: -아/어지다 goes with adjectives for a change of state; -게 되다 goes with verbs for a change in situation.
-게 하다 means making someone else do it.

items.register: Common when announcing news politely: 다음 달에 서울로 가게 됐어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: become, get (change of state, with adjectives)

contrasts.note: -게 되다 is for verbs and situations; -아/어지다 for adjectives.

items.commonMistake: ㅂ-irregular adjectives: ✗ 춥어졌어요 → ✓ 추워졌어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: be in a state (the result of an action remains)

contrasts.note: -고 있다 is an action in progress; -아/어 있다 is the state left after it (앉고 있어요 = sitting down, 앉아 있어요 = seated).

items.register: Used with verbs that don't take an object (앉다, 서다, 열리다, 붙다…).
items.commonMistake: ✗ 문이 열고 있어요 → ✓ 문이 열려 있어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.register: Very common in set phrases: 맛있게 드세요, 즐겁게 보내세요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -게 되다 is something that happens to you; -게 하다 is causing someone else to do it.

formation.example: 동생을 웃게 했어요 / 일찍 자게 해요

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: you know…, as you know (reminding the listener of something they know)

contrasts.note: -거든요 gives a reason the listener didn't know; -잖아요 points to something they already know.

items.register: Friendly in conversation, but can sound like 'obviously!' — careful with seniors.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: because, you see (giving a reason or background the listener didn't know)

contrasts.note: -잖아요 is for things the listener already knows.

items.register: Spoken only. Also used to set up a story before the main point: 어제 명동에 갔거든요. 그런데…
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: I see…, so … (realizing something, often from what you've just heard)

contrasts.note: -네요 is the everyday spoken reaction; -군요 sounds a bit more formal or written.

items.commonMistake: Present-tense verbs take -는군요: ✗ 가군요 → ✓ 가는군요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: I noticed / I found that… (reporting something you saw or felt in the past)
items.register: Conversational. Sounds natural when sharing impressions: 그 식당 정말 맛있더라고요.
items.commonMistake: Not for your own actions: ✗ (제가) 어제 영화를 보더라고요 → ✓ 어제 영화를 봤어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: while doing A, switch to B (A is interrupted or left)
items.register: With the past form it means A was completed, then B: 학교에 갔다가 집에 왔어요.
items.commonMistake: Same subject for both parts: ✗ 제가 자다가 동생이 왔어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: sets up background or a soft contrast ("…, so" / "…, but")

contrasts.note: -지만 is a plain 'but'; -는데 is softer and often just gives background before the main point.

items.register: Very common in speech. Ending a sentence with -는데요 softly invites a response or signals hesitation.
items.commonMistake: Action verbs take -는데: ✗ 가은데 → ✓ 가는데. Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ데: ✗ 좋는데 → ✓ 좋은데.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -(으)면서 is one person doing two things at once; with -는 동안 the subjects can differ.

items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -아/어서 is the everyday spoken reason; -기 때문에 sounds firmer and more formal.
-(으)니까 can be followed by a request; -기 때문에 can't.

items.commonMistake: No command or suggestion after it: ✗ 비가 오기 때문에 우산을 가져가세요 → ✓ 비가 오니까 우산을 가져가세요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: it must be / it would be … (a strong guess, often followed by concern or a suggestion)
items.register: Often caring: 배고플 텐데 먹어요. Also regret with -았/었으면 … -았/었을 텐데: 일찍 왔으면 좋았을 텐데.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: because of (something unexpected that led to a bad result)

contrasts.note: -아/어서 is a neutral reason; -는 바람에 stresses that the cause was sudden and the result unwanted.

items.register: The result part is in the past tense.
items.commonMistake: Verbs only, and no command after it: ✗ 바쁜 바람에 → ✓ 갑자기 일이 생기는 바람에.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.register: The second part usually has -도: 쌀 뿐만 아니라 맛도 있어요.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: tend to be, be on the … side
items.register: Softens a description of yourself or others: 저는 키가 큰 편이에요.

items.register: 먹을 만해요 can mean 'it's decent' rather than 'it's great' — tone matters.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: it seems (a guess from what you observe)

contrasts.note: -는 것 같다 can describe your own feelings or opinions; -나 보다 is only a guess about others or situations you observe.

items.commonMistake: Not about yourself: ✗ 제가 피곤한가 봐요 (unless you just realized it).
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.meaning: so that; to the point that
items.register: Often in polite instructions: 늦지 않도록 하세요 (Make sure you're not late).
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

items.commonMistake: Spaced as 온 지, and followed by a length of time: ✗ 온지 → ✓ 온 지.
items.source: Draft. Level and order follow the usual 초급/중급 textbook sequence; verify against 국제 통용 한국어 교육 표준 모형 (2017) and 한국어기초사전.

contrasts.note: -(으)려고 하다 is a firmer intention; -(으)ㄹ까 하다 is still undecided.

items.meaning: do completely (often with relief or regret)
items.register: The feeling comes from context: relief (숙제를 끝내 버렸어요) or regret (잊어버렸어요).
